title: Revit Modeling Practice
purpose: Implement governed modeling practice in Revit by limiting model detail to required uses, preferring reusable governed content, controlling in-place families, choosing groups/assemblies appropriately, and applying governed linked/workshared model structure.
preconditions: Applicable S2 information requirements and LOD/LOI expectations are known for the current project stage and intended use.
The project model breakdown, collaboration, and coordinate strategy are governed under S5/S6.
Applicable naming, parameter, material, and family standards are available.

steps.name: Model only to governed information need
actions: Model geometry and information only to the level required for coordination, documentation, safety, exchange, or other declared downstream use.
Avoid adding fabrication-level or visual detail that is not required by contract, information need, or approved coordination purpose.
Keep geometry, identity, and graphics aligned with the applicable naming, parameter, material, and view standards.
validation: Modeled detail can be traced to a declared information or delivery need.
Issued elements carry the information required for tags and schedules without manual patching.
failure_modes: Over-modeling increases complexity without a governed use.
Required LOI is replaced by manual annotation or disconnected data.

steps.name: Prefer governed reusable content
actions: Use approved loadable families and governed reusable content for repeatable components, standard equipment, vendor items, and scheduled/tagged content.
Use in-place families only for genuinely unique, non-repeating contextual conditions or temporary content where a reusable family is not appropriate.
Do not copy in-place content between projects to simulate a reusable library asset.
validation: Repeatable or scheduled content is implemented as governed reusable content unless an explicit exception applies.
In-place content has a documented rationale where required by project governance.
failure_modes: In-place families are used for standard repeatable content.
Project-specific geometry is copied between models instead of being governed as reusable content.

steps.name: Choose groups and assemblies by purpose
actions: Use model groups for repeatable multi-element design patterns that require coordinated repeated edits.
Use assemblies for built-up elements that require their own dedicated documentation views, details, or schedules.
Keep group scope manageable, avoid deep nesting, and apply governed naming.
validation: The selected construct matches its intended repetition or documentation purpose.
Groups are not used as uncontrolled whole-model containers.
failure_modes: Over-grouping or deep nesting creates editing/performance risk.
Assemblies or families would better serve the intended behavior.

steps.name: Apply governed linked versus workshared model strategy
actions: Use worksharing where multiple users author within the same governed model scope.
Use linked models to separate authoritative disciplines, systems, zones, or external consultant sources where ownership and release cadence must remain independent.
Maintain a directed, non-circular link structure.
Do not manually move linked models to compensate for unresolved coordinate governance.
validation: Model partitioning matches the governed S5/S6 breakdown and ownership intent.
Linked-model positioning follows the governed coordinate strategy.
failure_modes: A monolithic mixed-authority model is used where governed separation is required.
Circular or unmanaged nested linking is introduced.
Manual link offsets replace shared-coordinate governance.

steps.name: Document project-specific departures
actions: Record project-specific LOD/LOI, model breakdown, or modeling exceptions in the applicable BEP or governed project record.
Route deviations through the applicable approval authority rather than treating project preference as a standards change.
validation: Every material departure from the organizational rule is traceable to a project-specific governed decision.
failure_modes: A project-specific modeling choice silently redefines the organizational standard.

outputs: Revit authoring model aligned with declared information need and model-breakdown strategy
Governed reusable-content usage or documented exceptions
Traceable project-specific modeling departures where applicable
evidence: In-place family inventory and exception rationale where applicable
BEP or governed deviation record where applicable
governance_notes: Source phase-based LOD ranges were guidance, not promoted as fixed canonical project requirements.
The source's governance-parameter examples for in-place-family exceptions were not promoted because exact parameter definitions must come from S8 registry authority.
S5/S6 remain normative for model breakdown, federation, linking, and coordinates.

provenance.migration_note: Mixed normative/instruction source normalized to L6. Source examples, phase LOD ranges, and organization-specific labels were retained only as provenance context or omitted where not governed.
